faqs.q: What is the current position on Argentine import licensing?
faqs.a: It changes, so we confirm it per order rather than publish a description that ages badly. The import authorisation regime and the foreign-exchange approval that pays for the goods have both been revised more than once inside a single shipping cycle. At quotation we check where both stand, tell you plainly, and build the file to the regime actually in force — not to how the last shipment cleared.

faqs.q: Can you quote before our import authorisation is granted?
faqs.a: Yes, and the quotation will say plainly that it is subject to the authorisation. What we will not do is load a container against an authorisation nobody has checked and leave the consignment sitting at Buenos Aires while it is sorted out. Quote early, have the authorisation confirmed, then release the order — the sea leg starts only once the file is sound.

faqs.q: Does the foreign-exchange approval affect when the goods can sail?
faqs.a: Yes. The importer raises the foreign-exchange approval for the payment through their bank, and it needs to be in place before the vessel sails. We quote in US dollars because the approval is raised against the dollar value; quoting in another currency adds a step at your bank. Its current state is one of the two things we confirm at quotation, alongside the import authorisation.

faqs.q: How long does a container take from Jebel Ali to Buenos Aires?
faqs.a: Typically 35 to 45 days FCL from dispatch, sailing round the Cape of Good Hope and across the South Atlantic. Consolidated LCL with transhipment runs 42 to 55 days and suits small mixed orders. Air freight from Dubai into Ezeiza (EZE) takes 5 to 8 days with a connection, for a line that is down. Unusually, the freight is the predictable part of this lane and the licensing is the variable.

faqs.q: Can you deliver DAP to frac pads and bases around Añelo and Neuquén?
faqs.a: Yes. On DAP terms we deliver to the pad or the operating base at Añelo or in Neuquén. The road leg from Buenos Aires into the Neuquén basin is long — more than a thousand kilometres — so it is quoted rather than estimated, and fixed together with the sea freight so the delivered figure you compare is the real one. Tell us the operator's gate and site-access requirements at the order.

faqs.q: Which hose rating should we compare for Vaca Muerta frac and flowback duty?
faqs.a: Impulse life, not burst pressure alone. Stimulation work pressurises and depressurises a line over and over, and two hoses with the same burst rating can differ several-fold in cycle life depending on construction and how the ends were attached. Ask for the ISO 18752 or SAE J517 impulse performance explicitly; we quote against it where the manufacturer publishes it and say so where none does.

faqs.q: Which API wellhead and pressure-control equipment can you ship to Argentine operators?
faqs.a: We supply API 6A wellhead, API 16A BOP, API 16C choke and kill and API 7K drilling hose, with NACE MR0175 material documentation where the contract requires it. Makes we supply include TechnipFMC, Cameron (SLB), SPM, Anson, Stream-Flo and WOM. Monogram and material certificates are confirmed line by line at quotation, so the data book is settled before the order is loaded rather than at the Neuquén base.

faqs.q: What documents does an Argentine import from Dubai carry?
faqs.a: Five, in order: the import authorisation under the current regime, the foreign-exchange approval for the payment, the customs import declaration the importer lodges with Aduana before arrival, a Dubai Chamber attested certificate of origin, and material and test certificates where the order calls for them. Documents are in Spanish, with the description agreeing across the invoice, the packing list and the declaration.

faqs.q: Do you ship hose and valves for lithium brine projects in Salta, Jujuy and Catamarca?
faqs.a: Yes — hose, fittings and valves for brine extraction, pond transfer and processing plant on the Puna. Tell us the altitude, the brine chemistry and the night-time low, because the Puna combines thin air, abrasive dust, salt and wide temperature swings, and each one changes the cover, the seal compound and the fitting material. Delivery is DAP to site or CIF Buenos Aires for your own road haulage.

faqs.q: Do you supply cylinders and servo valves for the steel mills along the Paraná?
faqs.a: Yes — high-force cylinders, servo and proportional valves, high-pressure hose and fittings for tube, rolling and finishing lines in the Campana, San Nicolás and Villa Constitución corridor. Mill plant mixes metric, ISO and SAE connections, so send the nameplate data or the original part number and we match it rather than approximate. Delivery is CIF Buenos Aires or DAP to the mill gate.

faqs.q: Do you supply deck hydraulics for the fishing fleets of Mar del Plata and Puerto Madryn?
faqs.a: Yes — hose, fittings, cylinders and valves for deck cranes, trawl winches, net drums and steering gear. Marine duty wants covers that resist seawater and UV and fittings in plated or stainless material, so tell us where each line runs on the vessel. Orders ship CIF Buenos Aires for onward road haulage south, or DAP to the buyer's site when you want one delivered figure.

faqs.q: Is Cartagena or Buenaventura the right port for a delivery in Cali?
faqs.a: It is genuinely arguable, and we settle it against your delivery address at quotation. Cartagena is 32 to 40 days round the Cape and is clearly right for the coast, Bogotá and Medellín. Buenaventura is a short road leg from Cali but needs the Panama Canal on top of the Cape, at 44 to 56 days. For the Cauca valley and the south-west the Pacific usually wins once the road leg from the Caribbean is counted.

faqs.q: Which of our lines fall inside ICONTEC's regulated list?
faqs.a: ICONTEC is the certification body for Colombia's regulated products, and the list is defined — much industrial hose and fittings falls outside it. Where a line is inside, the conformity certificate from ICONTEC or an accredited body attaches to the product rather than the shipment, so it is obtained once and holds for future orders. We settle which lines are affected at quotation, before the container is loaded.

faqs.q: What does the importer need in VUCE before you ship?
faqs.a: An import registry entry raised through VUCE that covers every tariff line on the order. It is checked before anything else, because a registry that misses one line holds the whole consignment. Send the registry details with the purchase order and we match the Spanish descriptions on our invoice and packing list to it, so the declaration the importer lodges with DIAN before arrival agrees with the paperwork.

faqs.q: How long from Jebel Ali to Cartagena by sea, or to Bogotá by air?
faqs.a: Typically 32 to 40 days FCL from dispatch to Cartagena, sailing round the Cape of Good Hope; Barranquilla is the alternative on the same Caribbean coast. Buenaventura on the Pacific runs 44 to 56 days via the Panama Canal. Air freight from Dubai into Bogotá (BOG) takes 5 to 8 days with a connection, which is the option when a line is down. Documents are prepared before the vessel sails.

faqs.q: Can you deliver DAP to Llanos field bases at Yopal or Villavicencio?

The leg beyond Bogotá climbs over the Eastern Cordillera and is quoted rather than estimated, together with the sea freight, so the delivered figure is a real one. Tell us the operator's gate requirements and any site paperwork when you place the order.

faqs.q: Our equipment is North American — can you work from the OEM part number?
faqs.a: Yes, send the number exactly as printed. An original-equipment part number is a supplier catalogue reference, and it usually maps to something we hold under a different code; our replacement cross-reference covers a large set of manufacturer numbers. Where a number resolves to more than one candidate, the difference is normally seal material or seat angle, and we ask which applies rather than guess.

faqs.q: Which API and NACE documents can accompany wellhead equipment for the Llanos and Magdalena fields?
faqs.a: Manufacturer monogram and licence documentation, NACE MR0175 material documentation where the contract requires it, and material and test certificates from the mill or our test bench. We supply API 6A wellhead, API 16A BOP, API 16C choke and kill and API 7K drilling hose, in makes including TechnipFMC, Cameron (SLB), SPM, Anson, Stream-Flo and WOM. The document set is confirmed line by line at quotation.

faqs.q: Which hose holds up on the open-pit coal fleets of La Guajira and Cesar?
faqs.a: Hose with an abrasion-resistant cover and an impulse rating matched to the duty, because coal dust and heat wear covers faster than pressure alone suggests. We supply high-pressure hose, crimp fittings, couplings and made-up assemblies for haul trucks, shovels, dozers and drills, and for the rail and port loading that moves the coal to the coast. Tell us the machine and where each line runs; cargo lands on the Caribbean coast, the nearest gateway.

faqs.a: Yes, and turnarounds are where the sea lane earns its keep. Valves, gaskets, transfer and steam hose, fittings and lifting gear for a planned shutdown can be quoted from the work-pack list, batched and shipped once to Cartagena in 32 to 40 days, rather than bought piecemeal at short notice. faqs.q: Can you match spillway-gate and governor parts on older hydro plant in Antioquia?
faqs.a: Yes — cylinders, hose, fittings, valves and power-unit components for turbine governors, intake and spillway gates, and penstock valves. Hydro carries most of Colombian generation and much of it sits in Antioquia and along the Andean rivers, so delivery is usually CIF Cartagena with road haulage inland, or DAP to the plant. Send the nameplate data and existing part numbers and we match them rather than approximate.

faqs.q: Do you supply hydraulics for tunnelling and road works on the 4G concessions?
faqs.a: Yes — hose, fittings, cylinders and valves for excavators, drill jumbos, cranes and batching plants working the 4G road concessions through the cordillera. Tunnelling and mountain earthworks combine water, abrasion and high cycle counts, so tell us the machine and the duty. Fleets mix North American, European and Asian makes with different thread systems; send the part number or a photo of the fitting and we match it.

faqs.q: Why can a line that clears Peru or Chile without a certificate need one in Ecuador?
faqs.a: Because Ecuador applies INEN technical regulations across a broader list of products than its neighbours. INEN is Ecuador's standards body, and a line that clears Callao or San Antonio on a plain declaration can require a certificate of conformity here. So the part list has to be assessed against the Ecuadorian list specifically, not assumed from a neighbour — we do that at quotation and say which lines are affected.

faqs.q: When is the INEN certificate of conformity obtained?
faqs.a: At origin, before shipment — never at the pier. Discovering the requirement in Guayaquil means the goods sit while it is arranged six weeks from home. We assess each line against the Ecuadorian list at quotation, say which parts need a certificate from INEN or an accredited body, and run that work while the order is picked, so it adds no time to the lane.

faqs.q: How long by sea and air from Dubai to Guayaquil and Quito?
faqs.a: Typically 38 to 48 days FCL from dispatch to Guayaquil, sailing round the Cape of Good Hope and through the Panama Canal; consolidated LCL runs 46 to 58 days. Air freight from Dubai into Quito (UIO) or Guayaquil (GYE) takes 6 to 9 days with a connection, for a line that is down. Distance, not documentation, sets the timing on this lane.

faqs.q: Is Posorja or Guayaquil the better port for our container?
faqs.a: Guayaquil for most cargo. Posorja when its deep-water berth suits the vessel or the sailing schedule is better; it is a short road leg from there. Manta serves the northern coast and the Manabí fleet. We fix the port against the vessel and your delivery address at quotation, and the CIF figure is quoted to that port rather than to a default.

faqs.q: Can you deliver DAP to bases at Lago Agrio, Coca or Shushufindi?

Tell us the base's gate requirements and any site documentation when you place the order.

faqs.q: Can you pack an Oriente order for light aircraft or river craft?
faqs.a: Yes. Where the last leg is by light aircraft or river craft, dimensions and mass become the binding constraint, not cost. We can coil hose assemblies to a specified diameter, split a consignment into stated maximum package weights, and mark each package with its own contents so a partial delivery is still usable. Tell us the limits at the order rather than discovering them at the airstrip.

faqs.q: Does Ecuador's dollarisation simplify paying for an order?
faqs.a: Yes. Ecuador uses the US dollar and we quote in USD, so the quotation, the invoice and the settlement are the same money with no conversion anywhere in the transaction — a step most South American buyers have at their bank. The documents still need care: Spanish descriptions that agree across the invoice, the packing list and the importer's declaration.

faqs.q: What goes into the customs file for SENAE?
faqs.a: The importer lodges the customs import declaration (DAI) through SENAE before arrival. It is supported by our commercial invoice, a packing list in Spanish that matches the declaration line for line, a Dubai Chamber attested certificate of origin, INEN certificates of conformity for any regulated lines, and material and test certificates where the order calls for them. All of it is prepared before the vessel sails.

faqs.q: Which wellhead and pressure-control equipment can you supply for Oriente operators?
faqs.a: API 6A wellhead, API 16A BOP, API 16C choke and kill and API 7K drilling hose, with NACE MR0175 material documentation where the contract requires it. Makes we supply include TechnipFMC, Cameron (SLB), SPM, Anson, Stream-Flo and WOM. Monogram documentation and the INEN position of each line are confirmed together at quotation, so nothing in the data book or the customs file is left to the pier.

faqs.q: Do you supply hydraulics for the tuna fleet at Manta and shrimp processors on the Gulf of Guayaquil?
faqs.a: Yes — hose, fittings, cylinders and valves for purse-seine winches, power blocks, deck cranes and steering gear, and washdown-resistant hose and fittings for processing and packing plant. Seawater and washdown wear covers and plating fast, so tell us where each line runs; stainless fittings are worth specifying on deck. Manta takes cargo for the northern coast, Guayaquil and Posorja serve the gulf.

faqs.q: What wears hydraulic hose fastest at the Zamora Chinchipe copper and gold mines?
faqs.a: Rain, mud and abrasion, more than pressure. At the south-eastern operations around Mirador and Fruta del Norte, covers and fittings fail from wet grit long before the reinforcement does, so we specify abrasion-resistant covers and plated or stainless ends for haul trucks, loaders, drills and mill equipment. Give us the machine and the duty. Cargo usually lands at Guayaquil for road haulage, and DAP to the site gate is quoted rather than estimated.

What we compete on is the planned order — spiral hose, crimp fittings, flow iron and valve consumables held as real stock, quoted against a specification, batched and shipped once rather than flown in twice.

faqs.q: What do Stabroek contractors get held up on — customs or certification?

Guyana has no general pre-shipment conformity scheme and the customs file is short: the importer's declaration through the Guyana Revenue Authority, against our invoice and packing list, and an attested certificate of origin. What fails a consignment is the operator's specification — API monogram, NACE MR0175 material documentation, mill certificates traceable to heat number — so we confirm those at quotation, not at inspection.

faqs.q: How far ahead of the drilling programme should we place a Guyana order?

Separate the genuinely long-lead items for your equipment from commodity hose and fittings early — in a fast-growing basin the long-lead items bite every operator at once. We will say plainly which lines on your list fall into which category.

faqs.q: Should we fly parts into Georgetown for a vessel or rig breakdown?
faqs.a: For a line that is down, yes — air freight into Georgetown (GEO) takes 5 to 9 days with at least one connection. For anything else it undoes the reason to buy from Dubai at all: the saving is in the sea lane, and air freight spends it. If a part is needed in days rather than a week, a supplier in Trinidad or the US Gulf will usually be quicker, and we will say so.

faqs.q: Can rigging for a Demerara shore base go into service on arrival, certificates and all?

faqs.q: Which Brazilian enquiries is a Dubai supplier actually the right choice for?
faqs.a: Specification-driven ones, not routine replenishment. faqs.q: Is our hose line inside INMETRO’s scope, and is it certified per shipment?

faqs.q: Does our RADAR registration need to cover the tariff lines before you load?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the first thing we ask for. Brazil checks who is importing before what is being imported: the importer’s RADAR registration through Receita Federal, and any import licence (LI) through Siscomex that the tariff line requires, must cover the goods. If they do not, the consignment cannot clear however clean the rest of the file is, so we confirm coverage before the vessel sails.

faqs.q: Why is there no faster sea route from the Gulf to Santos than round the Cape?

Sites near Itaguaí or Vitória are usually served through Rio or Santos and a road leg, and we confirm the best routing at quotation. faqs.q: Does the free-port regime matter if our goods are staying in Uruguay?
faqs.a: No — it only matters for cargo moving on. The free-port regime lets goods be landed, stored, consolidated and re-dispatched at Montevideo without entering Uruguayan customs territory. If it is going on to Paraguay or Bolivia, it is the main reason to route through Montevideo at all.

faqs.q: Can Montevideo serve as the assembly point for cargo going on to Paraguay or Bolivia?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is often the right answer for the river markets. A consignment assembled under free-port storage and re-dispatched once travels better than several small ones arriving separately, each with its own paperwork. Uruguay is where a great deal of Paraguayan and Bolivian cargo is put together, and the free-port storage documentation is issued by the port operator on arrival.

faqs.q: Why must a transhipment through Montevideo be declared at quotation?
faqs.a: Because the documentation is different from the outset and the two routes are not interchangeable after the fact. A consignment declared for import and then re-exported is a far more expensive way to reach the same place than one documented for free-port storage from the start. Saying which applies at the order also lets us pack and label for a later break-down.

faqs.q: When is Nueva Palmira a better entry than Montevideo?
faqs.a: When the cargo is river-bound and the barge connection there beats trucking from the capital. Montevideo handles almost everything, including goods for Uruguayan sites and free-port consolidation. Nueva Palmira, at the mouth of the Uruguay river in Colonia, is used for cargo heading upriver, and we confirm the routing at quotation against the final destination.

faqs.q: What sea transit should we plan between Jebel Ali and Montevideo?

faqs.q: Can you supply hydraulics for the pulp mills at Fray Bentos, Paso de los Toros and Punta Pereira?

Tell us the equipment, fluid, pressure and temperature, and the shutdown date. Mill outages are planned well ahead, which suits a sea lane of five to six weeks; anything found during the outage can follow by air.

faqs.q: What does Uruguayan customs need for hose and fittings staying in the country?

The description has to agree across the invoice, packing list and declaration; material and test certificates are added where the order calls for them.

faqs.q: Is air freight into Carrasco an option for an urgent part in Uruguay?
